answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by anchoring each identity to one non-transferable, verifiable credential — like a quill that can sign only one name — issued once after a costly, independent check and bound to that agent's public key. Peers mirror this anchor before trading, refusing any second identity carrying the same credential. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must therefore pass a thousand separate costly checks and obtain a thousand distinct credentials, instead of copying one free identity at will.
